item.title: Jamie & Corinne Foxx Extend Fox Deal With Horror Series In Development
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Jamie and Corinne Foxx extend their studio deal through 2028 as they develop Buried, a horror series set in a Texas subdivision.
item.content:encoded:
Jamie Foxx and Corinne Foxx are taking a Texas ghost story to Fox.

Fox Entertainment Studios extended its deal with Foxxhole Productions through 2028, and the two sides are developing a horror series called “Buried,” Variety reported.

The new project draws on accounts from a subdivision in Crosby, Texas. Residents reported experiences they believed were hauntings, then learned their homes sat on land used for Black Hope Cemetery.

The burial ground served a Freedmen’s Town settlement.

Chad and Carey Hayes, who wrote “The Conjuring,” are executive producers alongside Jamie and Corinne Foxx.

Shelley Meals, whose credits include “It: Welcome to Derry,” will run the show and executive produce. Fox-scripted development executive Christina Porter will oversee the project.

“Foxxhole Productions is focused on bold, character-driven projects that are commercial, entertaining and often center Black voices and experiences,” Corinne, the company’s president, said in a statement.

Jamie signed the original first-look deal on March 5, 2025. Under the extension, Fox Entertainment Studios has the first chance to take on scripted comedy, drama and animation that he develops or executive produces.

Fox also has exclusive rights to his unscripted projects under the deal.

The agreement builds on a relationship that goes back to Jamie’s breakout on Fox’s sketch comedy series “In Living Color” in 1991.

Corinne later joined him on Fox’s “Beat Shazam,” where he hosted and she worked as the show’s DJ. Fox was already working with Jamie behind the camera when they signed the first deal.

He executive produced the network’s police drama “Alert: Missing Persons Unit,” as well as the music game show. On “Buried,” he and Corinne will share an executive producer credit.

Foxxhole has also worked outside scripted television. The company helped produce the Luther Vandross documentary, which traced the singer’s rise from singing backup to becoming one of R&B’s biggest solo acts.

The film, “Luther: Never Too Much,” premiered at Sundance in 2024. Jamie was already a Grammy-winning R&B performer himself, with records including “Blame It” and “Unpredictable.”

“Buried” is in development, and Fox has not announced a cast, series order or premiere date.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Diddy Gets Two Lawyers In Lil Rod Case As Deadline Hits
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Diddy has counsel again in Lil Rod's civil suit after two attorneys filed appearances at the end of a four-week deadline.
item.content:encoded:
Diddy has lawyers in his civil fight with Lil Rod again.

Adam Roland Rahman and Jonathan David Davis entered appearances for him in Manhattan federal court on November 19, the day his four-week window to find counsel or represent himself ran out.

Court documents reviewed by AllHipHop show Rahman’s notice first, followed by an extension request from Davis filed by Rahman. Davis then filed his own appearance.

U.S. District Judge J. Paul Oetken gave Diddy those four weeks after letting Sher Tremonte withdraw on October 22. The firm cited unpaid fees and trouble communicating with Diddy, and neither side opposed its request.

“Within four weeks of the date of this Order, Combs shall have new counsel appear or file a letter stating that he will appear pro se (that is, representing himself) with contact information,” Oetken wrote.

The order removed five lawyers from the case and directed the firm to send Diddy a copy by priority mail and email it to his power of attorney. The judge also told the clerk to remove Love Records and Combs Global Enterprises, which had already been dismissed from the case.

Lil Rod sued in February 2024 after working on Diddy’s The Love Album: Off the Grid. He alleged sexual assault and other misconduct during that work, allegations Diddy has denied.

Oetken dismissed the civil racketeering claims in 2025 but allowed parts of the suit to proceed.

Diddy later filed counterclaims, accusing Lil Rod of taking private footage and passing it along for use in a 50 Cent-produced Netflix documentary. Lil Rod moved to dismiss the counterclaims on September 17, before Sher Tremonte asked to leave.

As AllHipHop previously reported, Oetken gave Diddy until December 4 to oppose Lil Rod’s motion. That was already an extension from October 30, and the November 19 docket entries did not show a ruling granting the latest request for more time.

“If Combs does not file an opposition by December 4, 2026, the Court will construe Plaintiff’s motion as unopposed,” Oetken wrote.

item.title: Kanye West’s Terrified AI Vocal Accuser Can Stay Anonymous In Court Filings
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: A judge let an AI vocal producer sue Kanye West as John Doe in court filings while he seeks at least $220,000 for his work.
item.content:encoded:
Kanye West is being sued by a producer who can keep using the name John Doe in court filings, a Los Angeles judge ruled.

The producer says Ye and Yeezy Record Label LLC owe him at least $220,000 for work involving AI-generated vocals.

Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Kristin S. Escalante granted the limited request on November 18, MyNewsLA reported.

Escalante found Doe had “an overriding interest that overcomes the right of public access to court records, specifically, the right to be free from threats of harm and harassment.”

She gave the lawyers until November 30 to prepare a proposed final order for her signature.

Ye’s attorneys or a third party can ask Escalante to reconsider. The producer’s attorney, Mark Steven Avila, told the court that his client feared for his own safety and his family’s.

The request centered on identifying information while leaving the case itself public.

The decision follows an October hearing in which Escalante heard arguments and delayed a ruling. Doe had filed the lawsuit on August 3. He claims he received neither payment nor a written contract or credit for the work.

Doe alleges Ye’s team hired him on short notice in August 2024, just before the release of Vultures 2. He says he used recordings of his own voice to help create more than 400 vocal generations from at least 13 custom AI models.

The producer claims he contributed to five songs on Vultures 2 and two released songs tied to Bully.

He seeks at least $110,000 for the seven tracks and is asking the court to award twice that amount under Los Angeles’ rules for freelance work.

The city ordinance requires a written contract for covered work worth at least $600 and allows up to double the unpaid amount when a client fails to pay on time. Escalante’s ruling settles how the producer can be named in court papers for now, while his payment claim remains before the court.

item.title: Lil Jon Lands Grammy Nod After Pushing To Honor Late Son’s Studio Work
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lil Jon's Remix Meditation lands a Grammy nod as he seeks recognition for the recording work he shared with his late son.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Jon‘s push to honor his late son’s studio work now has a Grammy-nominated album behind it. Remix Meditation earned a place in the 2027 race after the rapper asked voters to recognize music Nathan Smith helped him record.

The Recording Academy lists Lil Jon as a nominee for Best Audio Book, Narration, and Storytelling Recording. The nomination follows his public campaign for Nathan, who worked as an engineer on his meditation projects.

In an interview on Reclaiming with Monica Lewinsky, Lil Jon explained how closely father and son worked together. Their bond extended beyond sharing a love of music into regular recording sessions, with Nathan helping capture his father’s voice.

“He was my engineer whenever I needed to record. We worked together a lot producing a lot of songs together,” Lil Jon told Lewinsky.

Lil Jon also used the conversation to ask Grammy voters to consider Remix Meditation. He connected that appeal directly to Nathan’s engineering work and his hope that his son could receive a posthumous honor.

The Academy’s public nominee listing names Lil Jon, not Nathan. Its rules allow certain credited engineers to receive a statuette if an entry wins, but the listing does not establish Nathan’s individual eligibility.

Under the 69th Grammy Awards rulebook, the category’s eligible producers and engineers or mixers must work on more than half the recording’s playing time. The rules distinguish those potential award recipients from the narrators or storytelling artists named as nominees.

Lil Jon’s earlier appeal for Nathan came while voters were choosing nominees. The new listing moves the album beyond that first-round campaign, with a winner still to be selected.

Nathan, who performed as DJ Young Slade, died at 27. Lil Jon recalled his son’s early remixes and graduation from New York University in the conversation with Lewinsky.

The album turns familiar Lil Jon songs into guided meditations, including reworked versions of “Get Low” and “Turn Down For What.” He developed the project with Kabir Sehgal after releasing earlier meditation recordings.

The category also includes recordings by Michelle Obama, Michael J. Fox, Dolly Parton, Tim Curry, and Paul McCartney with Morgan Neville.

item.title: Denzel Curry Plays DWNPLY And Records Three Songs For GTA VI
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Denzel Curry plays DWNPLY in GTA VI, records three songs as the character and joins N.O.R.E. and DJ EFN on Drunk Kings.
item.content:encoded:
Denzel Curry plays the rapper DWNPLY in Grand Theft Auto VI, and the role comes with three songs of its own. Rockstar Games’ credits list Curry in the main cast and on an in-game podcast. They also credit him under his own name on a separate track with 454.

The songs credited to DWNPLY are “Bulletproof Ski Mask,” “Pax,” and “Politik.” “Bulletproof Ski Mask” pairs him with the fictional rap duo Real Dimez. Cardo Got Wings, Yung Exclusive and Johnny Juliano produced it.

Murda Beatz produced “Pax,” while Take A Daytrip and Sophie Gray produced “Politik.” The credits list Curry as a writer on all three. His collaboration with 454, “FLA Flow,” appears under Denzel Curry rather than the character’s name.

Rockstar’s character guide gives the Real Dimez collaboration a backstory. The duo, Bae-Luxe and Roxy, have known each other since high school. They scored an early hit with DWNPLY and, five years later, are signed to Only Raw Records and looking for another one.

Rockstar credits Hood Brat and Krissy Celess as the performers behind Bae-Luxe and Roxy Rashad, respectively.

The podcast is Drunk Kings, one of the shows players can hear inside the game.

Rockstar credits Curry there as DWNPLY and lists N.O.R.E. and DJ EFN as themselves. The two are partners outside Vice City, too: they turned Drink Champs into a podcast network.

Curry comes from Carol City in Miami Gardens. In an interview on Bullseye, he recalled how fellow rapper Mike Dece introduced him to another artist from his neighborhood when he was 16.

“And then he shows me SpaceGhostPurrp, and then I found out Purrp was from Carol City, the same place I was from,” Curry told host Jesse Thorn. Curry went on to work with SpaceGhostPurrp’s Raider Klan before breaking out on his own.

The game takes place in Leonida, Rockstar’s fictional Florida, with Vice City as its stand-in for Miami. In its launch notes, Rockstar says players can listen to the game’s radio and podcasts both behind the wheel and on foot.

Grand Theft Auto VI launched November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

item.title: Erykah Badu Reunites With Rapsody For Soul Train Awards Cypher
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Erykah Badu will perform with Rapsody, CeeLo Green, Dave Hollister and Avery Wilson in the Soul Train Awards' Badu Cypher.
item.content:encoded:
Erykah Badu is bringing Rapsody back to the mic with her for the Soul Train Awards. The two won a Grammy together for “3:AM” last year, and they’ll share a cypher lineup with CeeLo Green, Dave Hollister and Avery Wilson.

BET announced the five performers on November 19. Badu is both producing and directing the segment, which the network is calling the Badu Cypher this year. Spotify is presenting it.

The lineup brings Badu back to a segment she helped launch. She was hosting the Soul Train Awards in 2015 when she got behind the turntables as DJ Lo Down Loretta Brown for the first Soul Cypher.

K-Ci, Chrisette Michele, Lalah Hathaway and Eddie Levert took turns singing that night, with Omar on keys.

The kickoff gave R&B singers a place to trade the mic in a format familiar to Hip-Hop fans. It became a fixture of the awards show. BET gave Badu its Legend Award at the same ceremony in 2018.

This time, Badu will appear alongside a rapper she knows well. The Recording Academy named “3:AM” Best Melodic Rap Performance at the 2025 Grammys, giving Rapsody her first career win.

Rapsody picked up another Grammy nomination this week. The Recording Academy nominated God Gotta Afro & Gold Hoops for Best Rap Album for its 2027 ceremony.

Badu also teamed with The Alchemist on Before the World Blows: The Abi and Alan Experiment, which came out in August.

CeeLo came out of Atlanta’s Goodie Mob before forming Gnarls Barkley with Danger Mouse.

Hollister sang with Blackstreet and lent his voice to Tupac Shakur’s “Brenda’s Got a Baby” and “Keep Ya Head Up.” Wilson went from competing on The Voice to playing the Scarecrow in Broadway’s The Wiz.

The awards show is returning to Chicago, where Don Cornelius started Soul Train. BET and the city partnered to stage the ceremony at the Harris Theater, and the broadcast will also mark the awards’ CBS debut.

The cypher is part of a bill that also includes a Freddie Jackson tribute. Anthony Anderson hosts the show, which airs November 27 at 8 P.M. ET/PT on BET and CBS.

item.title: Chloe x Halle Reunite As A Duo For Christmas Single
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Chloe x Halle return with a Christmas single after years of solo albums and guest appearances on each other's records.
item.content:encoded:
Chloe x Halle are putting both names back on the record. Chlöe and Halle Bailey announced “All I Think About on Christmas,” a holiday single due Friday (November 20), after spending much of the past few years making records under their own names.

“All I Think About on Christmas🎄out this friday 👭🏽,” the sisters wrote on their joint X account. The announcement comes a week after Chlöe put out A Chlöe Christmas, her seven-song holiday EP.

This time both sisters are billed as Chloe x Halle.

Going solo took some getting used to. Chlöe told Alex Cooper on Call Her Daddy that she began finding her footing as a solo artist while Halle was away filming The Little Mermaid. “I didn’t think I had worth or value without my sister,” she said.

The two kept recording together, though the songs came out under different names. On Chlöe’s Trouble in Paradise, Halle joined her for “Want Me.” Chlöe told Nylon that she asked her sister to make the most of a rare stretch in the same city: “Sis, we’re going to be in New York at the same time, I would love for you to be on the record.”

Halle took the vocal booth while Chlöe worked the soundboard. The following year, Chlöe returned the favor on “so i can feel again,” from Halle’s solo debut love?… or something like it. They’d also put their harmonies to work on the Bee Gees’ “To Love Somebody” for a 2024 Pandora campaign.

That back-and-forth goes back to the covers they posted on YouTube as kids. Their take on Beyoncé’s “Pretty Hurts” caught the singer’s attention and led to a deal with her Parkwood Entertainment label. Their last studio album together, Ungodly Hour, earned Grammy nominations for the album and for the songs “Do It” and “Wonder What She Thinks of Me.”

This year Chlöe made Resurrection with Timbaland, while Halle starred opposite Regé-Jean Page in You, Me & Tuscany. Halle played Anna, a woman who pretends to be engaged while staying in an Italian villa.

For now, the sisters have put one date on the calendar together: Friday’s Christmas single.

item.title: Ye’s 19-Year-Old “Graduation” Leads Daily Spotify Rap Streams, Chart Data Says
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Chart Data puts Ye's Graduation first in daily Spotify rap streams, 19 years after it beat 50 Cent to No. 1 on Billboard.
item.content:encoded:
Ye is back on top by a different measure, 19 years after beating 50 Cent in a first-week sales race. Music tracker Chart Data reported that Graduation was drawing more daily streams on Spotify than any other rap album.

A separate tally from Kworb, updated November 18, put the album at 5,071,582 daily plays and 9,822,427,992 total streams.

The daily figure measures one day’s listening. The lifetime count puts the album less than 180 million plays short of 10 billion. Chart Data reported the ranking without saying how long the album had been ahead.

AllHipHop reported last November that Graduation had passed 8 billion Spotify streams while drawing about 4.4 million a day. A year later, it is pulling in roughly 670,000 more plays per day than that earlier tally.

When Graduation first raced to No. 1, the numbers came from stores and downloads. Ye and 50 Cent released Graduation and Curtis on September 11, 2007.

Ye debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with about 957,000 first-week copies, while 50 Cent opened with 691,000. Graduation also sold 133,000 digital copies that week, a record at the time.

“This is a great day for Kanye West and Roc-A-Fella Records and a fantastic day for Hip-Hop and artistry,” Jay-Z told AllHipHop after the sales figures came in.

The then-Def Jam CEO said those sales showed the audience would turn out for music he considered sincere.

The Recording Academy awarded Graduation Best Rap Album at the 2008 Grammys. “Stronger” won Best Rap Solo Performance, while “Good Life,” featuring T-Pain, won Best Rap Song. “Stronger” also became Ye’s third No. 1 single on the Billboard Hot 100, following “Slow Jamz” with Twista and “Gold Digger” with Jamie Foxx.

Ye used his Best Rap Album acceptance speech to honor his mother, Donda West, who had died the previous November.

Ye is back in the Best Rap Album field for the 2027 Grammys with Bully – Deluxe, released through YZY/gamma.

The Recording Academy also nominated albums by Busta Rhymes, Cardi B, Rapsody, Don Toliver and Wale in the category.

The new nomination arrived the same week the album that won him that award in 2008 returned to the top of Chart Data’s daily Spotify rap tally.

item.title: Erica Campbell Gets Temporary Restraining Order After Unwanted Visits
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: A judge granted Mary Mary singer Erica Campbell a temporary restraining order after she reported repeated visits to her home.
item.content:encoded:
Erica Campbell obtained a temporary restraining order Wednesday after reporting repeated unwanted visits to her home. TMZ, which obtained her petition, reported the ruling.

“My kids are stressed and afraid to walk out the door,” the Mary Mary singer wrote in her petition. The request for court protection came after Campbell said she had hired private security and contacted Los Angeles police several times.

Campbell had already talked about the visits at California Worship Center, where she and her husband, producer Warryn Campbell, lead the congregation.

Speaking there the following week, Warryn said a woman had repeatedly claimed she was married to Erica. She said someone had slashed the family’s tires before church.

The couple took another car to the service, and Campbell later got a FaceTime call from her daughter about a woman in the backyard.

The singer shared footage from the family’s doorbell camera showing a woman at the entrance to their home.

In her account, it was not the first time the woman had come by. Warryn later told the congregation the visits had been going on since January and that the church’s security team already knew about her.

The Campbells began holding Bible studies in North Hollywood before opening California Worship Center.

In an interview on We Playin’ Spades, they talked with Nick Cannon and Courtney Bee about how they balance marriage, music and ministry. Warryn described how he went from producing records to becoming a pastor.

They’ve worked together on records as well. Warryn produced Mary Mary’s debut album Thankful, which included “Shackles (Praise You).” The sisters won their first Grammy for the album.

The Recording Academy lists Erica, Warryn and her sister Tina among the writers nominated for Mary Mary’s “Get Up.” Erica later recorded “Help” with Lecrae and appeared this year on Skilla Baby’s “Strength in Numbers,” with Warryn among the song’s writers.

Warryn said the woman had also turned up at services more than once. Authorities have not publicly linked her to the damage to the Campbells’ tires.

Campbell said she told her daughter to leave the house and come to church.

item.title: Kool DJ Red Alert Explains Why He Turned Down Cash From Artists
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kool DJ Red Alert tells Tony Yayo and Uncle Murda why he turned down cash from artists and told them to book him instead.
item.content:encoded:
Kool DJ Red Alert had an answer for artists who wanted to give him money: book him for a gig instead.

The New York radio veteran told Tony Yayo and Uncle Murda he turned down cash from artists because he didn’t want anyone to say he’d taken their money.

“I get my blessings another way,” Red Alert said in an interview on The Real Report. He was open to getting paid for a job he actually did.

“Put me on, have me do an event,” he said, offering that as an alternative to taking a gift.

Even if a gift was meant as a thank-you, he said the person handing over the money could tell a different story later and make it sound like they’d paid him off.

“I’m not going to give you a reason,” he said.

On 98.7 KISS-FM, that judgment could help a record reach listeners well beyond the club where he first heard it.

One of the records he didn’t pass up was “South Bronx.” Red Alert recalled hearing DJ Raul play the Boogie Down Productions track at Latin Quarter and the crowd erupting as Raul played it again.

Scott La Rock handed him the record to play on the radio. Red Alert said he aired it on his Saturday show, cutting in with the Bronx record when MC Shan’s “The Bridge” reached its chorus.

Red Alert went on to give early airplay to Queen Latifah, A Tribe Called Quest and Black Sheep, according to WBLS. He also toured with Boogie Down Productions and the Jungle Brothers, bringing his work behind the turntables to stages beyond New York.

The DJ is marking 50 years behind the turntables at his November 24 Sony Hall gala. Teddy Riley and WBLS’s Bugsy are hosting, with DJ Jazzy Jeff, Kid Capri and DJ Spinna on the bill.

Red Alert’s four-hour farewell broadcast is scheduled for November 30 on 107.5 WBLS.
